description.en: Setup now runs welcome → pair this device → optionally create a first agent, and pairing alone counts as finished. Agents created there, and those created by the Marketplace's install wizard — which now offers "Connect to <workspace>" by default — join the workspace as they are created instead of ending up local-only.

title.en: Removing a workspace now unpairs this device from it

description.en: Removal used to delete the launcher's own record only, leaving the device paired: the workspace kept listing it, kept it online, and could still create agents on it. Removing now also deletes this device's pairing and credential on the server and takes its agents out of the workspace. Deleting the workspace for every member stays a separate checkbox in the same dialog.

title.en: Workspace connection problems now say what happened

description.en: An agent bound to a workspace this device is no longer paired with reports a missing workspace credential instead of an unexplained authentication error, and a workspace that removed this device says so on its card rather than going quiet. Agents on workspaces the device was never paired with are marked as legacy connections.

title.en: Workspaces are joined with a pairing code

description.en: "Add workspace" opens straight on the pairing form: paste the eight-character code from the workspace and this device joins it — one device can hold several workspaces, each with its own code. The launcher no longer creates a workspace and no longer accepts a workspace link or invitation token; both registered a workspace this device was never paired with, a state the daemon can no longer obtain credentials for. Create a workspace on the web after signing in, then join it from here. Workspaces already on this device keep working.

title.en: Each device holds its own workspace credential

description.en: Pairing issues a credential for this device alone. Rotating a workspace's token no longer disconnects paired devices, and re-pairing keeps running agents online.
